etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *mata. First cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 五 (MC nguX). Compare modern Hokkien 五 (gō͘ / gǒ͘).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the classical lower bigrade verb (ラ行下二段活用) わかる (wakaru). Cognate with 別(わか)れる (wakareru) and 分(わ)ける (wakeru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Nominative form of 切(き)れる (kireru, “be cut off, be injured”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Likely from Old Japanese. First attested in isolation with unambiguous phonetics in 950. Also attested in compound verb sashihasamu in the Kojiki of 712, but the relevant section of text is written in kundoku (a kind of written Classical Chinese read out in Japanese) in the ideographic spelling 刺挟, and the phonetic realization as Japanese is not clearly attested until later.
Derivationally, this appears to be Old Japanese root pasa (modern hasa) + verb-forming suffix む (mu, “seem like, look like; treat like; make like”). Root pasa may be a kind of ablaut cognate with poso as reflected in modern adjective 細い (hosoi, “narrow”), and adverbs 細々 (hosoboso, “narrowly”, iterative, repetitive), ほっそり (hossori, “narrowly, skinnily”, stative). Root pasa is also reflected in modern noun 稲架 (hasa, “frame for drying sheaves of harvested rice”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Less common alternative spelling of compound verb 差し挟む (sashihasamu).
Listed as the only spelling in some references, not listed at all in others. May be avoided due to the resulting ambiguity with the homographic 挟む (hasamu) reading.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From the 受身形 (ukemikei, “passive form”) of 生む (umu, “to give birth to”), hence the meaning "to be born".
Also attested in its Classical Japanese form 生まる (umaru), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 編 is a daiyōji replacing 篇.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 飾(かざ)る (kazaru, “to decorate, to adorn”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
Shift from Old Japanese 大人 (opobito, “boss, chief”, literally “big person”).
/opobito/ → /obito/
